body.name: Operational Excellence Programme
body.description: Northwind 2027 flagship programme to modernise manufacturing operations across the Leeds and Rotherham plants — warehouse automation, predictive maintenance and supplier risk management.
body.goal: Reduce unplanned downtime by 30% and cut warehouse handling cost per unit by 20% by end of 2027.

initiatives.name: Scrap Reduction Programme
initiatives.summary: A focused programme on the five largest scrap codes, each with an owner, a baseline and a weekly countermeasure review.
initiatives.business_value: Converts avoidable material loss directly into margin without new capital.
initiatives.expected_roi: Estimated GBP 470k annual saving, confirmed against the August finance baseline.
initiatives.problem_statement: Scrap at 3.4% of material cost against a 2.1% benchmark is about GBP 640k a year of avoidable loss.
initiatives.deliverables: ["Scrap baseline pack by code","Countermeasure register with owners","Updated standard work for the affected operations"]
initiatives.success_criteria: ["Scrap reduced from 3.4% to 2.4% of material cost within twelve months","Every one of the five codes with a measured baseline and named owner","Countermeasures embedded in standard work, not held as actions"]
initiatives.scope_in: ["Top five scrap codes across both sites","Measured baseline per code and named owner","Weekly countermeasure review","Standard work updates arising from the countermeasures"]
initiatives.scope_out: ["Supplier-caused defects (covered by Supplier Quality Gate)","Capital equipment replacement","Packaging and transit damage"]
initiatives.key_risks: ["Two of the five codes span both sites and need joint ownership","Countermeasure capacity competes with the MES rollout in the first quarter"]
initiatives.title: Scrap Reduction Programme
initiatives.description: Scrap ran at 3.4% of material cost in 2026 against an industry benchmark of 2.1%, which is roughly 640 thousand pounds a year of avoidable loss. The request is for a structured reduction programme built on the top five scrap codes, each with a named owner, a measured baseline and a countermeasure reviewed weekly. It deliberately avoids a site-wide campaign in favour of five focused problems that can be closed. Finance confirmed the material cost baseline in August and the steering committee approved the programme in September; delivery starts in January.

initiatives.name: Unify MES Cycle Count and Retrofit Controllers
initiatives.summary: Adopt a single MES cycle-count definition and retrofit two controllers to ensure auditable OEE measurements on Line 3, addressing the current unauditable cycle count issue.
initiatives.title: Unify MES Cycle Count and Retrofit Controllers

initiatives.name: Implement Predictive Maintenance Using Spindle History
initiatives.summary: Utilize the existing ten-year spindle condition history to establish a predictive maintenance pipeline, aiming to reduce unplanned spindle downtime by 30%.
initiatives.title: Implement Predictive Maintenance Using Spindle History

initiatives.name: Energy Monitoring and ISO 50001
initiatives.summary: Sub-metering of the twelve largest loads, energy per production hour, and ISO 50001 certification.
initiatives.business_value: Protects two of the three largest accounts where certification is a tender requirement.
initiatives.expected_roi: Payback in 21 months on energy savings, before any revenue protection is counted.
initiatives.problem_statement: 14.2 GWh a year is metered at four points only, so no department can be held to an energy budget.
initiatives.deliverables: ["Sub-metering installation","Energy reporting pack by department","ISO 50001 management system manual"]
initiatives.success_criteria: ["ISO 50001 certificate awarded at first audit","Energy per production hour reported monthly by department","Energy cost per unit reduced by 8% within twelve months of go-live"]
initiatives.scope_in: ["Sub-metering on the twelve largest loads across both sites","Energy consumption per production hour by department","ISO 50001 energy management system documentation","Certification audit preparation"]
initiatives.scope_out: ["On-site generation or solar investment","Building fabric improvements","Scope 3 supply chain emissions"]
initiatives.key_risks: ["Certification body lead time may push the audit past the tender deadline","Metering installation on the main incomer needs a planned shutdown"]
initiatives.title: Energy Monitoring and ISO 50001
initiatives.description: Northwind buys 14.2 GWh a year across the two sites but meters it at four points, so no department can be held to an energy budget. This initiative installs sub-metering on the twelve largest loads, publishes consumption per production hour, and uses the resulting evidence base to certify the energy management system to ISO 50001. Certification is a customer requirement in two of the three largest accounts and is expected in the next tender round. The board approved the business case in July on the condition that the metering data is available before the certification audit is booked.

initiatives.name: Digitize Wakefield Goods-In Inspection
initiatives.summary: Transition the Wakefield goods-in inspection from paper to a digital quality gate, reducing the detection lag of supplier nonconformances and improving schedule reliability.
initiatives.title: Digitize Wakefield Goods-In Inspection

initiatives.name: Automate Short-Stop Capture on Line 3
initiatives.summary: Implement automated short-stop capture at controllers to accurately log and address the largest OEE loss bucket, reducing reliance on memory-based reconstructions.
initiatives.title: Automate Short-Stop Capture on Line 3

initiatives.name: Warehouse Automation Pilot
initiatives.summary: Goods-to-person shuttle for the 400 fastest-moving SKUs in one Leeds aisle, sized to prove the business case.
initiatives.business_value: Reduces handling cost per unit and frees floor space for the growing order book.
initiatives.expected_roi: Payback in 26 months at pilot scale; shorter if wave 2 proceeds.
initiatives.problem_statement: Handling cost per unit rose 11% in two years while order lines grew only 4%; picking walks the full aisle.
initiatives.deliverables: ["Shuttle installation and commissioning","Revised replenishment rules","Measured pilot result pack for the wave 2 decision"]
initiatives.success_criteria: ["Cost per pick in the pilot aisle reduced by 20%","Pick accuracy maintained at or above 99.6%","Business case for wave 2 evidenced by measured data, not vendor claims"]
initiatives.scope_in: ["One aisle of the Leeds finished-goods store","Goods-to-person shuttle for the top 400 SKUs","Reworked pick face and replenishment rules","Measured before-and-after cost per pick"]
initiatives.scope_out: ["Remaining three aisles (wave 2, subject to the pilot result)","Raw material store","Outbound transport planning"]
initiatives.key_risks: ["Vendor lead time for the shuttle is 22 weeks and already committed","Peak season overlaps the commissioning window"]
initiatives.title: Warehouse Automation Pilot
initiatives.description: Handling cost per unit in the Leeds finished-goods store has risen 11% over two years while order lines have grown only 4%, because picking still walks the whole aisle. This pilot installs a goods-to-person shuttle for the fastest-moving 400 stock keeping units and reworks the pick face around it. The pilot deliberately covers one aisle only, so the business case for the full store can be measured rather than assumed. If the measured saving holds, wave 2 extends the shuttle to the remaining three aisles in 2027.

initiatives.name: Skills Matrix and Upskilling
initiatives.summary: A live skills matrix for 340 production roles, feeding shift planning and closing eleven single points of failure.
initiatives.business_value: Removes single points of failure that currently stop a cell when one person is absent.
initiatives.expected_roi: Avoided downtime from absence cover, estimated at 90 production hours a year.
initiatives.problem_statement: No single record of machine sign-off; cover for absence is arranged from memory and eleven roles have no backup.
initiatives.deliverables: ["Skills matrix covering every production role","Upskilling schedule agreed with the works council","Shift planning procedure update"]
initiatives.success_criteria: ["Zero production roles without a trained backup","Skills matrix refreshed within one working day of a sign-off","Shift planners using the matrix as the source for cover decisions"]
initiatives.scope_in: ["Skills matrix for all 340 production roles","Link to existing HR training records","Upskilling plan for eleven single points of failure","Matrix as an input to weekly shift planning"]
initiatives.scope_out: ["Office and engineering roles","Replacement of the HR system","Apprenticeship programme design"]
initiatives.key_risks: ["The Q4 shift pattern review may change the role structure the matrix is built on","Training capacity competes with the order book in the run-up to year end"]
initiatives.title: Skills Matrix and Upskilling
initiatives.description: Northwind has no single record of who is signed off on which machine, so cover for absence is arranged by memory on the shift. This initiative builds a skills matrix for all 340 production roles, links it to the training records already held by HR, and schedules the upskilling needed to remove the eleven single points of failure identified in the 2026 audit. The matrix becomes the input to shift planning rather than a document that is refreshed once a year. Work is currently on hold while the Q4 shift pattern review runs, because training slots cannot be booked against a rota that is about to change.
initiatives.blocked_reason: Paused until the Q4 shift pattern review concludes. Training slots cannot be booked before the new rota is agreed with the works council.

initiatives.name: Predictive Maintenance for CNC Line
initiatives.summary: Condition-based maintenance on Leeds CNC cells 1-6, replacing the fixed 12-week service calendar.
initiatives.business_value: Recovers production hours lost to unplanned stoppages and reduces premium transfers to Rotherham.
initiatives.expected_roi: Payback in 14 months on avoided downtime and reduced expedited freight.
initiatives.problem_statement: Unplanned CNC stoppages cost 640 production hours in 2025 and are invisible until the machine stops.
initiatives.deliverables: ["Sensor installation on six CNC cells","Condition-monitoring dashboard for the shift engineers","Alert-to-work-order integration","Response runbook and training record"]
initiatives.success_criteria: ["Unplanned CNC downtime reduced by 30% against the 2025 baseline","At least 80% of alerts confirmed as genuine by the shift engineer","Mean time to repair reduced from 5.2 to 3.5 hours"]
initiatives.scope_in: ["Leeds CNC cells 1-6 (vibration and spindle-current sensing)","Condition-monitoring model and alert thresholds","Work-order trigger into the existing maintenance planner","Shift engineer training and response runbook"]
initiatives.scope_out: ["Rotherham CNC cells (planned for wave 2)","Replacement of the maintenance planning system itself","Press shop and assembly equipment"]
initiatives.key_risks: ["Sensor cabling requires cell downtime that competes with the order book","Alert thresholds too sensitive in the first weeks, eroding operator trust"]
initiatives.title: Predictive Maintenance for CNC Line
initiatives.description: Unplanned stoppages on the Leeds CNC cells cost Northwind an estimated 640 production hours in 2025, and every stoppage pushes work to the Rotherham site at a premium. This initiative fits vibration and spindle-current sensors to cells 1 to 6 and streams the readings into a condition-monitoring model that raises a work order before a bearing fails. Maintenance planning moves from a fixed 12-week calendar to a condition-based schedule agreed with the shift engineers. The first two cells run as a controlled pilot so the alert thresholds can be tuned against real failure data before the rollout continues.

# Preventive Maintenance Policy 2026.pdf

Preventive Maintenance Policy 2026
Northwind Manufacturing Ltd. - Engineering and Maintenance
Approved by the Operations Board, 28 January 2026
1. Policy statement
Northwind Manufacturing Ltd. operates a planned preventive maintenance regime across all
three UK sites. Reactive repair is treated as a failure of the plan, not as a normal mode of
working. Every unplanned stoppage longer than thirty minutes is reviewed and the maintenance
plan is updated accordingly.
2. Asset criticality
Assets are classified into three bands.
Band Definition Minimum regime
A Single point of failure for a
customer-facing line
Condition monitoring plus
monthly planned intervention
B Capacity constraint with a
workaround
Quarterly planned
intervention
C Redundant or non-constraint Annual inspection
Line 3 at Rotherham, the outbound shuttle at Leeds and the precision cell at Wakefield are band
A assets for 2026.
3. Planning rules
1. Planned maintenance windows are agreed with production planning eight weeks ahead
and are protected. Releasing a window to production requires the written agreement of
the Operations Director.
2. Spare parts for band A assets are held to a minimum of one set on site.
3. A work order is raised for every intervention, including inspections that find nothing.
4. Maintenance technicians record actual intervention time. Estimated time is not accepted
as a completion record.
4. Measures
The policy is measured by unplanned downtime hours per line per month, preventive plan
adherence and mean time between failures for band A assets. The 2026 target is unplanned
downtime below four percent of available production hours on every line.

-- 1 of 2 --

5. Competence
Every technician working on a band A asset holds a current competence record for that asset.
Competence records are reviewed twice a year. Where a task can be performed by one person
only, the gap is logged on the skills matrix and a cross-training action is raised.
6. Review
This policy is reviewed annually by the Operations Board, or earlier if a critical safety event or a
repeat band A failure occurs.

-- 2 of 2 --

# UK Discrete Manufacturing Benchmark 2026.pdf

UK Discrete Manufacturing Performance
Benchmark 2026
Prepared for Northwind Manufacturing Ltd.
Reference study, published June 2026
Summary
This benchmark compares Northwind Manufacturing Ltd. against a reference set of forty-one
UK discrete manufacturers with turnover between GBP 40 million and GBP 120 million and
between two and five production sites. The reference set is drawn from the same industrial
classification and was surveyed between January and May 2026.
Headline positions
Measure Northwind Reference median Upper quartile
Overall equipment
effectiveness
61 percent 68 percent 76 percent
Unplanned downtime
as share of available
hours
7.4 percent 5.1 percent 3.2 percent
On-time in-full
delivery
88 percent 93 percent 97 percent
Inventory turns 5.2 6.8 9.1
Scrap and rework
cost as share of
revenue
3.1 percent 2.2 percent 1.3 percent
Training hours per
full-time equivalent
per year
11 18 27
Interpretation
Northwind sits below the reference median on every headline measure. The largest single gap is
inventory turns, where the company holds roughly thirty percent more working capital in stock
than the median comparator of the same size.
The unplanned downtime position is the gap with the clearest route to improvement. Two thirds
of the reference set that moved from the third quartile to the median did so by protecting planned
maintenance windows rather than by capital investment.

-- 1 of 2 --

The training position is a leading indicator rather than a lagging one. Companies in the upper
quartile for training hours were, on average, two years ahead of the median on the adoption of
shop-floor digital tooling.
Method and limitations
Data was self-reported and normalised to a common definition of available hours. Sites with
fewer than twenty employees were excluded. Comparators were not adjusted for product mix, so
companies with a high proportion of low-volume, high-variety work will read lower on overall
equipment effectiveness for structural reasons.

# Goods-In Inspection SOP-QC-014 (rev 4).pdf

Goods-In Inspection Standard Operating
Procedure (SOP-QC-014)
Northwind Manufacturing Ltd. - Quality Function
Revision 4, issued 12 March 2026
1. Purpose
This procedure defines how incoming materials are received, inspected and released at the
Leeds, Rotherham and Wakefield sites of Northwind Manufacturing Ltd. It replaces revision 3 of
February 2025 and is mandatory for all goods-in operators and quality inspectors.
2. Scope
All purchased raw material, bought-in components and subcontracted parts entering any
Northwind site, including free-issue material supplied by a customer. Consumables below GBP
250 per delivery are excluded and follow the light-touch route in section 7.
3. Responsibilities
Role Responsibility
Goods-In Operator Booking in, visual check, quarantine
placement
Quality Inspector Sampling, dimensional verification, release
decision
Head of Quality Concession approval, supplier escalation
Supply Chain Lead Supplier corrective action follow-up
4. Procedure
1. Confirm the delivery against the purchase order line and the advance shipping note.
2. Record the supplier batch number and the Northwind goods receipt number in the quality
tracker before the pallet leaves the receiving bay.
3. Place the delivery in the yellow quarantine zone. Material must not be moved to free
stock until a release decision is recorded.
4. Apply the sampling plan in Appendix A. For suppliers on enhanced surveillance the
sample size doubles until three consecutive deliveries are accepted.
5. Verify the critical characteristics listed on the inspection card. Record actual measured
values, not pass or fail marks.

-- 1 of 2 --

6. Where a nonconformity is found, raise a supplier nonconformance report the same
working day and photograph the defect before any rework.
7. Record the release decision, the inspector identity and the timestamp. The batch record
must allow a finished-goods defect to be traced back to the incoming batch.
5. Records and retention
Inspection records are retained for seven years. Photographs supporting a nonconformance report
are retained for the life of the supplier agreement plus two years.
6. Escalation
A supplier with two accepted-with-concession deliveries inside a rolling quarter is escalated to
the quarterly supplier review. A supplier with a critical safety-related nonconformity is
suspended immediately pending a containment plan.
7. Light-touch route for low-value consumables
Visual check and quantity confirmation only. No quarantine placement is required, but the goods
receipt number and supplier batch remain mandatory fields.
8. Related documents
 QP-02 Control of Nonconforming Product
 QP-07 Supplier Approval and Surveillance
 WI-QC-031 Use of the Coordinate Measuring Machine

-- 2 of 2 --

initiatives.title: MES Rollout Line 3
initiatives.description: Rotherham Line 3 still reports production on paper travellers that are keyed into the ERP the following morning, so schedule adherence is always a day old. This initiative deploys the manufacturing execution system already running on Lines 1 and 2 to Line 3, including station terminals, barcode traceability and automatic downtime capture. Planners gain live order status and the quality team gains a per-unit genealogy record they can pull during a customer audit. The rollout is sequenced around the summer shutdown so that no confirmed customer order is put at risk.

tasks.title: Agree the MES downtime reason-code taxonomy
tasks.description: Quality and Operations use different downtime vocabularies; the MES needs one agreed list.
tasks.acceptanceCriteria: One signed reason-code list published to both departments.

tasks.title: Configure the MES work-order interface to ERP
tasks.description: Map work orders, routings and material issues between the MES and the ERP production module.
tasks.acceptanceCriteria: Ten test work orders flow end to end without manual correction.

tasks.title: Install shop-floor terminals on Line 3
tasks.description: Mount and network the eleven ruggedised terminals along Line 3, including the two packing stations.
tasks.acceptanceCriteria: All eleven terminals reachable from the MES server with under 50 ms latency.

tasks.title: Validate barcode traceability at the packing station
tasks.description: Prove that a finished pallet can be traced back to batch, machine and operator in one query.
tasks.acceptanceCriteria: Traceability query returns batch, machine and operator for twenty sampled pallets.

tasks.title: Write the Line 3 cutover runbook
tasks.description: Hour-by-hour plan for the switch from paper travellers, including the rollback point.
tasks.acceptanceCriteria: Runbook reviewed in a dry run with the shift leads.

tasks.title: Migrate paper travellers for the top twenty part numbers
tasks.description: Rebuild the twenty highest-volume travellers as MES routings and retire the printed copies.
tasks.acceptanceCriteria: Twenty routings released in MES and the paper masters withdrawn from the line.

tasks.title: Commission the MES-to-SCADA data bridge
tasks.description: Stream machine states and cycle counts from the Line 3 SCADA layer into the MES.
tasks.acceptanceCriteria: Machine state changes appear in the MES within five seconds for eight hours of running.

tasks.title: Sign off the MES acceptance test pack
tasks.description: Formal acceptance against the forty test cases agreed with the vendor.
tasks.acceptanceCriteria: Forty test cases passed and countersigned by the vendor.

tasks.title: Define the OEE calculation rules with Quality
tasks.description: Fix availability, performance and quality definitions so the Line 3 OEE figure is comparable across shifts.
tasks.acceptanceCriteria: OEE definition sheet approved by the Head of Quality.

tasks.title: Train Line 3 operators on the MES terminal
tasks.description: Two-hour hands-on session per shift, with a short competence check at the end.
tasks.acceptanceCriteria: Every Line 3 operator has a signed competence check on file.
